text:
alice_support: Customer A reported sudden 403s on /v1/generate after a scheduled service key rotation ~2h ago. They shared two request IDs: req-0a1b2c3d and req-5f6e7d8c. Asking for repro steps and whether this is a token chaining issue.
charlie_sre: can you paste the original curl they used + redwood headers (mask secrets) and the exact timestamps? also which cluster/region? @dana_prodeng FYI
alice_support: region=us-west-2, cluster=redwood-uw1, timestamps: 2026-03-12T14:23:11Z (req-0a1b2c3d), 2026-03-12T14:24:02Z (req-5f6e7d8c)
alice_support: here's the curl they ran (token redacted):
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_SERVICE_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Org: 98765" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Project: 43210" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-v1","input":"hello"}'
```
alice_support: they said it worked before rotation, started failing immediately after. No retries, single attempt each time.
charlie_sre: looks like org/project headers are present. Do we have evidence of a stale key cache on the edge? please collect the proxy request log for those req ids, and also the auth service logs around the rotation window. I want the signed header + derived key id.
dana_prodeng: collecting auth-service logs now. Also: did the customer use a service token chained from a user token, or a short-lived delegated token? that can cause 403 if scope mismatch.
alice_support: customer said they used a service token minted by our portal 3h earlier. They didn't mention delegation. I asked them to run a local repro with our public endpoint using the same headers; requested a curl they can run with an expired placeholder to reproduce header shape.
alice_support: shared lightweight repro for them to run (no real token):
```
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}s" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer PLACEHOLDER" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Org: 98765" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Project: 43210" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-v1","input":"test"}'
```
charlie_sre: once you have the proxy trace, attach the `auth.signed_headers` and `auth.key_id` fields. if the key_id on the incoming request doesn't match the rotated mapping, that's our smoking gun. Also request the debug bundle: headers, raw response body, full curl -v output, and the exact server time.
alice_support: asked customer to run the repro and to send full `curl -v` output + `systemctl status redwood-agent` output from their side. also asked for the `sig` header value (they can redact signature itself).
deploy-bot: FYI: service-key rotation completed 2026-03-12T12:05:00Z across us-west-2, rollout id rot-20260312-11
dana_prodeng: got auth logs up to 2026-03-12T15:00:00Z. preliminary: two incoming requests show key lookup failure -> auth returns 403 with reason=KEY_SCOPE_MISMATCH. attaching snippet:
```
[2026-03-12T14:23:11Z] req=req-0a1b2c3d auth_lookup key_id=sk_live_OLD -> not found in project 43210
[2026-03-12T14:24:02Z] req=req-5f6e7d8c auth_lookup key_id=sk_live_NEW -> scope mismatch: allowed_org=11111, got_org=98765
```
charlie_sre: OK that matches an org/project mapping race during rotation. Next steps: ask customer to confirm the org header they're sending is 98765 (they said yes). We'll repro by creating a temporary key scoped to org=98765 and run same curl from our lab. Also check edge cache TTL for key mapping; set to 30s currently.
alice_support: forwarded this to customer with next-action steps and ETA ~2h for root-cause repro. asked to DM logs if they see additional req ids. :thumbsup:
